decision: NARROWED BEYOND UNKNOWN-TARGET INTERVENTIONAL COARSENING IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: directly learning an abstract causal DAG from interventional data is prior art
recovering a causal partition without first recovering the fine-grained DAG is prior art
unknown intervention targets do not by themselves require language
partition-refinement and intervention-descendant signatures can identify a non-language causal coarsening
coarse target recovery, abstract-DAG accuracy, task success, and post-hoc human-readable labels do not identify raw-language equivalence or semantic denotation
counterexample: Two models related by simultaneous permutation or within-block recoding of recovered coarsening parts, abstract-DAG node labels, target blocks, raw-utterance classes, denotation, language encoder, policy, and decoder preserve the complete observational and interventional law, intervention-descendant signatures, RePaRe decisions, abstract graph, task metrics, and language-conditioned predictions while assigning different utterance equivalence relations and semantic target partitions. Fine targets with identical intervention signatures remain unidentifiable inside the same recovered block unless an externally fixed language contrast breaks the residual automorphism.
official_code_status: paper-specific official code verified with uv.lock, hash-pinned requirements, tests, Snakemake workflow, and reported CPU reproduction commands; exact commit SHA was not exposed by the available connector, so immutable execution is not yet claimed; README blob pinned
